Retired people have been increasing in numbers, nowadays. This stage of life is believed to be given support financially by the government, however, there are others who think that they need to finance their needs and should not expect any government assistance. Both of these views need to be discussed further as I believed that these retired individuals are important members of the society and should be given support from authorities for as long as they need them. 


Many of the retired people are receiving pensiones from their previous work in different sectors that offered insurance policy. This financial support sometimes comes from the government’s insurance system if they had worked for the government sector such as public teachers, soldiers, and other government office employees. In this regard, it is axiomatic that the government should support retired people because they had rendered service for a period of time.


Meanwhile, there are retired people who were not able to establish financial security at their old age. These are the ones who worked menial jobs, or unfit to work at all. In this case, there are government authorities who make sure that these individuals are taken care of under a social service unit. Rendering care to these people is a government responsibility in order to build a humane society. 


However, a part of the society is not keen on the idea of government helping the retired ones. This is due to the fact that some of them are still physically and mentally able to work. Others also claim that their families, especially children should take responsibility for financing their needs. For instance, in Filipino culture, the elderly are well supported by their family members and some children even include them in their paid insurances, such as medical care. 


All these being said, the government needs to allocate budget for social services to retired persons who do not have any support from private sectors or their own families. These retired members of the society have rendered in their own way a service to their nation and thus should be respected and supported in their needs.

Looking at the chart more closely, one can see that the largest age group comprises 16 to 24-year-olds and that it grew steadily from 2010 to 2015, gradually reaching nearly 70 percent. In contrast, the oldest group, made up of people 75 years and over, consistently have the lowest rate of all five age groups. They surged initially, increasing from 10 percent in 2010 to 20 percent by 2011. However, this figure eventually settled into a slow increase, increasing to 20 percent by 2015. It is noteworthy that people from 55 to 64 years old remaind stable during the whole period. Over the past decade, by virtue of advanced living standards, the educational system has gained popularity in various countries, leading to a paradigm shift in the application of multiple subjects at schools. This, therefore, is believed to be beneficial for learners. Despite the many positive ramifications that may derive from the argument, this educating style is likely to be predominantly disadvantageous to students due to the rationales outlined below. 

Admittedly, advocates of the statement that adolescent students should better learn a variety of subjects at schools may argue that this implementation not only offers learners many useful skills but also enables a foreseeable well-rounded individual. First, when attending to some intellectual subjects, namely chemistry or math, students are able to enhance their cognitive abilities. Some examples of this, particularly include the improvement of problem-solving skills like balancing chemical equations or addressing chemical reactions. Second, since a multi-subjects educating style is implemented, this necessitates a well-developed citizen. By studying many majors at schools, students might get a deeper insight into every aspect of life, leading to a complete understanding of their future.

Nevertheless, despite the feasible positive impacts above, focusing on some chosen subjects is still the optimal choice. First, favorite majors act as incentives for youngsters’ passion and motivation in learning. It should be remembered that once adolescents are encouraged to engage in the fields they are interested in, they will have opportunities to foster their talents and potential abilities themselves, therefore minimizing teachers’ efforts in terms of helping learners understand the lessons. In addition, once students can select their favored subjects, a self-learning style will be granted. If young learners can make a decision on what they will study, their independence and autonomy skills in learning will be ensured, leading to a responsible individual later on. 

In conclusion, despite the ubiquity of multi-subject avenues in education, prioritizing several selected subjects remains the most preferred choice due to the autonomic and favorable features. Because of these merits, I do expect government development aims to be drastically altered in the foreseeable future.

Because of this, most streaming platforms like Spotify and Apple Music include features that help artists control their music distribution and monetization. Therefore, it's almost impossible to pirate music now, unlike in the 2000s.

On the one hand, technology can amplify the wealth gap as affluent individuals and well-funded corporations can employ automation and artificial intelligence in the workplace. This allows them to reduce labor costs, leading to job displacement and wage stagnation for the working class. For instance, in manufacturing, advanced robotics and automation can replace human workers, leading to job loss and downward pressure on wages, while the companies get the benefits of cost savings and increased profits. This automation-driven wealth accumulation can leave many individuals and communities struggling to keep up economically.

On the other hand, technology can be a powerful tool in reducing income disparities. The digital revolution has made information and education more accessible. The advent of e-learning platforms and open-source educational resources allows individuals from economically disadvantaged backgrounds to acquire valuable skills, enhancing their employability. Additionally, technology facilitates innovative solutions to societal issues, exemplified by telemedicine, which provides cost-effective healthcare options to underserved communities, effectively bridging the healthcare disparity. The widespread use of smartphones has also created opportunities for micro-entrepreneurship and access to financial services, empowering individuals to improve their economic well-being.

In conclusion, the impact of technology on the wealth gap is a complex and multifaceted issue. Its potential to either widen or narrow the wealth gap depends on how we approach its development and distribution, emphasizing access, education, and opportunities for all.

It is reported that natural forest area continues to decline, marine ecosystems are undermined severely, and countless species are suffering from illegal poaching. Hence, there are increasing voices that question the necessity and viability of making a change.

Governments could promote a greater understanding of plants and animals by investing in the research and preservation efforts of universities, zoos, and botanical institutes. This may ensure the survival of individual species and produce tangible benefits in the form of new medicines and products. 

An alternative strategy would be to protect natural habitats by expanding nature reserves. This would have immediate positive consequences for those areas by preserving delicate ecosystems. The most effective solution is to limit the damage at the source. Companies that engage in practices that harm the environment should be required to demonstrate that they have taken all reasonable efforts to minimize the damage. Public contracts for roads and buildings should only be awarded to firms that have a good environmental track record. The strategies outlined above could do much to reverse the destruction that threatens the world’s plants and animals. 

To conclude, a planet being pushed to the edge will eventually turn on us. 

With the accelerating rate of mass extinctions of plant and animal species, I believe, effective measures should be taken immediately to make a difference.

I believe some kids enjoy doing art, others might feel uncomfortable. Hence, I would like to suggest that school can make these courses optional. prompt.text: Some people believe that it is the government's responsibility to provide care and financial to support people after they retire. Others, however, think that individuals themselves saving money in their own care when they are old. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

essay.text:
The issue of retirement support is a topic of contention, with compelling arguments presented on both sides. Some advocate for government-funded financial assistance and care for citizens following their retirement, while others insist on individual responsibility in planning and saving for retirement.

Proponents of government-provided retirement support assert that it aligns with principles of social justice. They highlight the fact that numerous individuals may struggle to accumulate sufficient savings for their retirement due to a myriad of factors, including meager wages, mounting medical bills, and unforeseen financial burdens. Government-sponsored support is seen as an essential mechanism to ensure that retirees can enjoy a decent quality of life during their post-employment years.

For instance, Singapore's administration has implemented a Central Provident Fund (CPF) scheme. The CPF operates as a mandatory savings initiative for employed Singaporeans and their employers. When these workers eventually retire, they can tap into their CPF savings to finance their retirement years.

On the contrary, adversaries of government-backed retirement support argue that it is inequitable to obligate taxpayers to finance the retirement of others. They contend that governmental management of financial resources is not always the most efficient approach.

Moreover, some contend that government-provided retirement support may have a disincentivizing effect on personal financial responsibility. They point out that when people are aware of government guarantees, they may be less inclined to proactively save for their retirement.

For instance, studies have indicated that individuals residing in nations with extensive government-provided retirement benefits exhibit a reduced inclination to independently save for their retirement.

In my perspective, it is imperative for the government to play a role in furnishing retirement support to its citizens. Nonetheless, I firmly believe that individuals should take responsibility for their retirement planning and savings.

One strategy to strike a balance between these two objectives is to institute a universal retirement savings accounts system. Under this system, all employed individuals would be mandated to contribute a portion of their income to dedicated retirement accounts. The government could then provide matching contributions for low- and middle-income earners. This approach would guarantee that every individual has a fundamental level of retirement savings.

Furthermore, the government should offer tax incentives and employ other means to motivate people to save for their retirement. Additionally, the government could provide financial advisory services and educational resources to empower individuals to make informed decisions about their retirement planning.

By adopting such a well-rounded approach, governments can facilitate the assurance of a secure and comfortable retirement for all citizens.

prompt.text: Some people believe that the government should continuously support the development of arts. Others believe that the money can be well spent on scientific research. Discuss both and give your own opinion.

essay.text:
Arts and sciences both contribute significantly to a country’s prosperity in the modern world, but which one is worth more funds still remains controversial. While some people believe that the government should spend continuously on arts, I would argue that the government’s budget should be planned more carefully and in some cases, scientific research definitely needs more money.
 
Some people think that arts should be funded in a continuous way because this can enrich people’s cultural life and possibly they can have better moods every day. If the spending on the film industry increases, film-makers will be able to produce films of higher quality to entertain the viewers, and after watching an entertaining film, these people will definitely be happier. In addition, some musical instruments can also be installed in public places with sufficient budget, and people who want to play them can feel free to do that. Both the players and the listeners will benefit from this.
 
On the other hand, scientific research is also indispensable as with higher technology, people can have a better quality of life, especially in some deprived countries. The investment in genetic engineering can increase the yields in agriculture by inventing new hybrid crops, and people naturally will not suffer from hunger any more. Finally, the research in the areas of communications technology such as the Internet can reshape people’s lives, as they will be able to get richer resources faster and many new technologies will also appear as a result of it.
 
In my view, the government’s expenditure on arts is not likely to improve people’s living standards significantly and for countries whose citizens are still struggle with a basic standard of living, the investment in scientific research should be considered first, as this is more practical and can solve some urgent problems about people’s daily life domestically.

For example, soldiers working in the army retire younger and find themselves jobless after retirement. It is argued that heads of enormous organizations should receive higher wages due to their crucial responsibilities, whereas others believe that this creates an unfair environment for labourers. This essay will explore both viewpoints prior to concluding that I agree with the former perspective.

On the one hand, a number of individuals argued that creating an equal working environment is critical for a variety of reasons. Firstly, having equal pay would create a sense of comfort among labourers which would enable them to do their tasks received from their supervisor without any related burden. Additionally, managers do not virtually contribute more actual value than their employees. For example, managers of cattle breeding firms do not directly participate in production processes and therefore, there is no reason for them to receive higher profit than typical employees.

However, I believe that it is more beneficial to offer competitive wages to directors of large organizations. First and foremost, high-income act as a motivator for these individuals to achieve their targets and enhance their management skills. For instance, companies like Google or Apple offer high earnings for leadership positions, which helps retain top talent. Furthermore, supervisors with rich experience can adapt to changes in the workplace and manage employees more effectively than others, and as a result, they deserve an adequate wage.

In conclusion, while it is critical to maintain equality in terms of wages in large businesses, I believe that pay should be based on individuals' experience and level of responsibility. Consequently, offering higher salaries to supervisors is necessary to retain talent and ensure the effective management of huge organizations.

To recapitulate, I firmly reiterate that even though ordinary staff members perform a lot of laborious work, companies do not hold them accountable for their failure. essay.text:
For some time now, it has become a topic of debate as a section of the society believes that paying excessively to senior most staff of an organization is completely acceptable, whereas others hold a view that this is not fair to the junior workers. In my opinion, I completely agree that a huge compensation to executives should be regarded positively.

On the one hand, many have valid arguments against higher salaries to executive level employees. First and foremost, everyone in a firm works around 9 hours a day, that is the reason everyone should be paid accordingly. This is because as per the IT markets' standard, employees on each level have to clock atleast 45 hours per week regardless of their positions and Infosys is the prime example of this. Besides this, without any effort of workforce on lower positions, seniors can not drive a company because most of the technical work is done by the juniors and higher level employees just deliver that to clients. Furthermore, employees with less experience have also invested a prodigious amount of money and time to acquire the required experience and educational degree; thus, attractive salaries to seniors is not a fair process followed by companies.

On the other hand, people who advocate the view that a higher salaries to directors and VPs have certain reasons behind their thinking. Firstly, running a firm smoothly requires a team of workers with extensive experience and knowledge about different industries to deal with numerous international clients and to crack any deal in no time. These senior-most people have been working in different sectors since ages so their experience and work commitments should be compensated with handsome salaries. Besides this, if a director fails at any point of time means the entire organization would suffer. Mahindra Satyam, for example, has a similar story where CFO failed to run the company as a result, lower staff had to suffer as they were terminated. Therefore, I wholeheartedly agree that attractive remuneration to directors is completely fair and the right approach.

To conclude,  although many still argue that paying excessive salaries to the top-most worker is unfair to juniors, I am completely convinced that this is definitely a fair option as these people are behind running the business properly and due to this the workers on lower positions are earning.

Some people believe that studying at university or college is the best route to a successful career, while others believe that it is better to get a job straight after school.

Discuss both views and give your opinion.

essay.text:
Society is divided on the notion that youngsters should pursue higher education after  finishing high school. While I am convinced that obtaining proper qualifications from respective institutions is essential, I believe that we should contemplate the opposite view thoroughly as well. 

Firstly, continuing their studies right after school can give students many advantages. These include being able to study better while they are young and the momentum is still there. Additionally, they would be able to graduate at a young age and get into the workplace early, meaning that they have a better chance of excelling in their careers with many future career prospects. Nowadays, these qualifications are critical in the process of acquiring their dream profession. The majority of white-collar professions, for instance, cannot be easily obtained without having those certain degrees. Therefore, students should continue their studies, provided that they would like to secure a rewarding career. 

On the other hand, many believe that  adolescents should secure a job right away once they finish high school. While this may be true for many careers where certain skills can be acquired during practical work such as car mechanic or construction work, it might not be the case for areas where theoretical skills are crucial in the learning process, for instance, psychology and medical fields need intensive research and knowledge that can only be achieved with the guidance of teachers with expertise in those fields.

In conclusion, while it may be true that some occupations prioritize work experience, the majority of high-paying jobs these days require certain higher educational degrees. Hence, the idea that adolescents should get a job right after the academy is harmful to the youth and may limit their future career opportunities.
